func_800240DC_24CDC.title: Read a game flag
func_800240DC_24CDC.summary: Tests one bit in the game's packed flag bank at D_8015C608_15D208. Returns zero when the flag is clear, or the bit mask when it is set. Use this to query progression, encounter, and event state without changing it.
behavior: For a nonnegative flag ID, the function selects byte (flag_id / 8) & 0xFF, then ANDs it with 1 << (flag_id & 7). Consequently a set bit can return 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128. The native return is not a normalized Boolean.

The bank covers 256 bytes, or 2,048 bit positions. The native implementation masks the byte index rather than validating the input. IDs at or above 0x800 alias earlier bytes; negative arguments follow the compiler's signed division and remainder path and are not meaningful public inputs.

Boss synchronization queries encounter-active, defeated, and reward flags. Extra Options uses the same reader to gate boss acceleration while the encounter is paused or inactive. Reading a bit does not execute the event associated with it.

parameters.name: flag_id
parameters.description: Bit index into the game flag bank. Pass a known game flag in the range 0x000–0x7FF, not a byte offset or bit mask.

func_800240DC_24CDC.returns: Zero if clear; the nonzero bit mask if set. Compare the result with zero.
cautions: Do not compare a set flag with == 1; flags whose bit position is not zero return larger masks.
The native function does not bounds-check IDs. Confirm what a flag controls before relying on it.
func_800240DC_24CDC.exampleExplanation: This wrapper validates the bank range and normalizes the native mask to 0 or 1. The game owns the flag bank; the wrapper only reads it.
func_800240DC_24CDC.decompilationNote: Live Ghidra decompilation of resident address 0x800240DC, captured 2026-09-04. Displayed logic is simplified for nonnegative IDs; the native function also contains signed division/remainder adjustments.

evidence.note: Flag reader declaration and encounter-state use.
Room and paused-flag gates before accelerating the boss.

func_80024038_24C38.title: Set a game flag
func_80024038_24C38.summary: Sets one bit in the packed game-flag bank without changing the other bits in that byte. Native event logic and multiplayer boss synchronization use this entry point to record progression or encounter state.
behavior: For valid nonnegative IDs, selects byte (flag_id >> 3) & 0xFF and ORs it with 1 << (flag_id & 7). Setting an already-set flag leaves the bank unchanged.

The multiplayer mod attaches an entry hook to this function to observe native flag writes and coordinate boss defeat behavior. Direct writes to the flag bank bypass that function hook; reaching the same stored bit is not necessarily equivalent from a mod's perspective.
This routine only changes a bit. Its decompiled body does not save to storage, spawn a reward, or finish a boss death animation.
cautions: There is no native bounds check; larger IDs alias the 256-byte flag bank.
Progression flags can affect later game logic. Set only flags whose meaning and required event sequence you have established.
func_80024038_24C38.exampleExplanation: Call from game logic with a documented flag ID when the associated event is actually complete. This helper validates the range, but does not perform the event or persist a save.
func_80024038_24C38.decompilationNote: Live Ghidra decompilation of resident address 0x80024038, captured 2026-09-04; simplified for valid nonnegative IDs.

evidence.note: Native flag-set entry hook used by boss synchronization.

func_80024088_24C88.title: Clear a game flag
func_80024088_24C88.summary: Clears one bit in the packed game-flag bank, preserving other flags. Boss synchronization clears selected native death or reward flags so the local encounter can finish its own visual sequence.
behavior: For a valid nonnegative ID, reads byte (flag_id >> 3) & 0xFF and ANDs it with the inverse of 1 << (flag_id & 7). Clearing a clear flag has no additional effect.
Boss synchronization uses this operation with encounter-specific checks and retained local state. Clearing a completion bit alone does not restore an actor or reconstruct an encounter.
cautions: IDs are not bounds-checked by the native routine.
Do not treat this as a generic boss reset: actor state, room state, and other progression bits can remain changed.
func_80024088_24C88.exampleExplanation: Use with a documented transient flag in a game-state transition you control. The range check does not establish that clearing a particular flag is appropriate.
func_80024088_24C88.decompilationNote: Live Ghidra decompilation of resident address 0x80024088, captured 2026-09-04; simplified for valid nonnegative IDs.

evidence.note: Clears Congo's reward flag while retaining local lethal-hit state.

D_800C7AB2.title: Current game room ID
D_800C7AB2.summary: The game's 16-bit current room identifier. Mods read it to limit behavior to a particular room, invalidate cached actor state after a transition, and keep multiplayer actors in the same game room.
behavior: Extra Options checks this value against each encounter's room constant before changing boss behavior. Team Up remembers the last value and resets follower state when the room changes. Multiplayer stores this value beside tracked actors and rejects actors or pending effects associated with a different room.

This is an in-game room identifier, distinct from the multiplayer server's user-entered Room ID. Equality with a room constant only identifies the room; actor readiness and encounter phase need their own checks.

The current sources declare the storage as both signed short and unsigned short. Both are 16-bit for the mod target. Treat room IDs as unsigned for comparisons and serialization, and use a consistent declaration within each translation unit.
cautions: Reading a new room ID does not prove that its actor data has finished loading. Check native lifecycle and resource readiness separately.
Writing the variable directly is not a supported room-transition recipe. The engine manages additional transition state.
D_800C7AB2.exampleExplanation: Tracks room transitions after the system update and increments a mod-owned generation counter. Cached native actors should be discarded or revalidated when the generation changes.

evidence.note: Follower lifecycle detects room changes using this value.
Signed declaration and Goemon House room gate.
